title: Fix Lowpoly End To End Boot
description: Get lowpoly working end-to-end. Fix module resolution error: Failed to resolve module specifier @bytecodealliance/preview2-shim/cli in plugin worker boot.
summary:
Fixed two root-cause bugs blocking lowpoly's react dev boot (and every other technology's, since both live in the shared `@semio-tech/framework-os-dev` pipeline):

1. `rewritePreview2ShimImports` in framework/product/os/dev/script.ts used a substring guard (`content.includes("@bytecodealliance/preview2-shim/")`) that also matched its own rewritten output, so `rewriteExistingPluginShimImports()` (called on every dev/build) progressively double-rewrote every plugin's transpiled `*_component.js`, corrupting the `@bytecodealliance/preview2-shim/*` import into paths like `../_vendor/../_vendor/.../cli.js.js` — exactly the "Failed to resolve module specifier" error this ticket reported. Fixed by anchoring the regex to `from ['"]@bytecodealliance/preview2-shim/...['"]`, which no longer matches an already-rewritten relative import. Verified idempotent across repeated rebuilds for lowpoly and other previously-corrupted plugins (cad, puzzle).
2. Once (1) was fixed, booting `dev:lowpoly` with `SEMIO_RENDERER=react` still crashed: Vite failed to load `framework/product/os/dev/js/vite.config.ts` because it transitively imports `../script.ts`, which had a top-level `import { Database } from "bun:sqlite"` — Vite's config loader can't resolve the `bun:` scheme even under Bun. Fixed by making the `bun:sqlite` import lazy (dynamic `import()` on first use) instead of a static top-level import.
3. Also found and fixed: `framework/product/os/dev/script.ts`'s trailing `await runBundleScriptMain(...)` ran unconditionally on import (not just when the file is the process entrypoint), so merely importing `semioBackboneVitePlugin` from `vite.config.ts` re-triggered the whole CLI router against Vite's own argv, throwing "unknown command". Fixed by guarding it with `if (import.meta.main)`, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the repo (e.g. framework/plugin/registry/script.ts).

Verified: `bun run dev:lowpoly` with `SEMIO_RENDERER=react` (port 6078) now boots end-to-end — plugin builds and transpiles cleanly, Vite starts, and the served page / main entry module / lowpoly plugin JS, wasm, and vendored preview2-shim assets all resolve with HTTP 200 via curl (no console/tooling access to a real Chrome instance was available in this environment, so pixel-level UI verification wasn't possible, but the server logs show a clean boot with no thrown errors, matching the exact failure this ticket reported). `bunx vitest run` in framework/renderer/react passes (28/28). Confirmed via git stash that `cargo test -p lowpoly-plugin` fails identically with and without this change (pre-existing, unrelated: the crate's `plugin_exports!` macro requires the wasm32/p2 target and can't be cargo-tested natively) — not introduced by this work.

lowpoly's Rust plugin (lowpoly/plugin/rs/lib.rs) already implements full feature parity with the premigration `lowpoly/react/index.tsx` (mesh view, hover/select/gumball/marquee, Model/Paint window engagements, UV canvas) via the shared `framework/renderer/react` host — that generic architecture is intentional post-migration and was not the gap; the gap was purely this boot-pipeline breakage.
